world.bio: I worked as a teaching assistant in a primary school in Didsbury for eight years. After my own first birth went badly (long induction, an emergency section, and no one explaining what was going on) I decided to train as a birth doula. I'm halfway through my DONA-accredited course and have started taking my first clients in South Manchester. Mum to a toddler, W, who started nursery this month.
skills_assets: Birth doula training (DONA pathway), 4 of 6 modules done, reading list and case log in progress
Eight years of experience with children and parents, patient and calm in tense rooms
A birth bag: birthing ball, TENS machine, massage oils, rebozo, laminated position cards
Local network: two independent midwives in Chorlton, a hypnobirthing teacher, a postnatal physio
Good at writing, run a small Instagram for the practice (87 followers)
A car and flexible childcare with my mum on Tuesdays

projects.name: Whitlow Doula (practice setup)
projects.text: Setting up as a sole trader. Have a logo, a one-page contract, a pricing plan at £600 for antenatal + birth support + postnatal visit. Two clients so far, both due in December and January. Insurance still needs sorting.

projects.name: Bathroom renovation
projects.text: Redoing the family bathroom on a tight budget: stripped the wallpaper myself, tiler can't come until the 20th. Currently washing in the sink. Husband says it'll be done by Christmas, I say Christmas which year.

notes.text: W's first full week at nursery and she's already caught a cold. Runny nose, croupy cough. Up at 3 for her. I know it's normal but I'm shattered and this is exactly the week I'm supposed to be revising the antenatal module.

Client meeting with L. (due 14 Dec). We talked for two hours about her birth preferences. She asked whether induction at 41 weeks is something she can say no to, and what the hospital's policy on water birth is. I said I'd find out and couldn't say anything more than 'it's your decision'. After, in the car, I realised I didn't actually know what the local policy was. I felt hopeless and fraudulent.

Read the DONA scope of practice again. We don't give medical advice. We don't diagnose. We help people get information, we don't give it. But where's the line between 'telling you what the NICE guideline says' and 'advising'? I keep going round this. Afraid of crossing it, afraid of being useless on the other side.

Reading group night. We were supposed to read Hamnet, I read the first fifty pages. Five of us ended up talking about someone's divorce and finishing two bottles of white. It was lovely. I came home and checked on W and she was sleeping with her bum in the air.

Second client, R., due in January, asked about the Maternity Voices Partnership and what to do if she wanted a water birth and her midwife was against it. Said I'd check. Reached out to my doula tutor, she said 'ask your local midwife contacts'. I don't have any local midwife contact who has time for me.

Budget for bathroom: £2,800. Tiles £450, vanity £320, plumber £600, rest unknown. Husband wants a heated towel rail, I said the towel rail costs more than my first month of doula income. He laughed. I wasn't joking.

Remembering my own birth. The consultant said 'we'll just have a quick look' and then I was in theatre. No one told me why. My husband says I'm over-processing. I say I'm processing at last. This is what I want to do for others: to be the person who says 'this is what is happening, and this is what you can ask for'.

Instagram post about birth positions got 40 likes, one DM from a stranger asking if I'm a midwife. I wrote back that I'm a doula and explained the difference. She said 'oh, so what can you actually do?' I answered, but my reply felt so small.

messages.text: Mum: How's W's cough? Me: Bad but she's eating. Mum: Give her honey. Me: She's under 2, no honey. Mum: Since when? Me: Since NHS guidance. Mum: In my day...
Jen: Did you do the case log? Me: Half. Jen: My clients keep asking clinical stuff. Me: Mine too. I freeze. Jen: Same. We need a midwife friend. Me: I know.
Tom: Plumber says Tuesday. Me: Can you be there? Tom: I've got a client call. Me: I've got a booked consultation. Tom: Mum could? Me: She's got W. Tom: Right.
L.: Did you find out about the water birth policy? Me: Not yet, I'm checking with a few people. L.: No worries, just wanting to be informed. Me: I'll get back to you this week.

relations.about: Husband, software tester, supportive but hands-off with the bathroom
Retired school secretary in Stockport, looks after W on Tuesdays
Course buddy in Leeds, same worries about clinical scope

constraints: Tuesdays only for childcare, must be home by 6
Tight budget: practice income so far £0 while bathroom and nursery fees run
Won't give medical advice, anxious about scope of practice
Cannot be on-call until module 6 is signed off
sensitive: Her own traumatic first birth drives her into this work
Anxiety that she is not qualified enough and clients will realise
